pr_body:
This PR optimizes `EXTRACT(year/month/day FROM date/timestamp)` through caching.

The main observation here is that, while DuckDB supports a very wide range of dates (from the years `5877641 (BC)` to `5881580`) - almost all dates/timestamps used in practice lie within a narrow range of that domain (`1970 - 2050`). This only amounts to `29584` days that are practically relevant. We can optimize the computation significantly by computing the date part for all of these days in advance, and doing a look-up in the cached array - falling back to the slow implementation only if the date does not lie within this domain. The cached array only has a size of ~`60KB` when storing 2 bytes per day.

This PR implements this through the `DateLookupCache`.

Benchmark (running on TPC-H SF15):

```sql
select count(*) from lineitem where extract(month from l_shipdate)=6;
```

| v1.0.0 |  New  |
|--------|-------|
| 0.16s  | 0.07s |
pr_comments:
> Fixes #12491 ?

It speeds up that query by a significant amount indeed

issue_context.title: Linear scan filters are much slower than expected
issue_context.body:
### What happens?

I am seeing very slow filter scans compared to a very simple (not vectorized) for-loop over a very simple column store implementation.

### To Reproduce

Here is one example:
```
INSTALL tpch;
LOAD tpch;
CALL dbgen(sf = 15);
.timer on
SELECT L_SHIPINSTRUCT FROM lineitem WHERE extract('month' FROM L_SHIPDATE) = 6;
```
This query takes on the order of seconds for single-threaded, and hundreds of milliseconds for multi-threaded:
```
single-threaded:     3.613s, 1.366s, 1.340s
multi-threaded (8): 0.427s, 0.209s, 0.231s
```

I have an example column store implemented that is just a C++ tuple of std::vectors. A simple for loop (no vectorization) produces the following runtimes:
```
single-threaded:      0.854s, 0.305s, 0.282s
multi-threaded (8):  0.230s, 0.165s, 0.140s
```

This gets worse with larger scaling factors, e.g. sf=25
```
duckdb (single):        6.435s, 5.786s, 5.480s
duckdb (8 threads):  3.656s, 3.576s, 3.737s
my scan (single):       1.861s, 0.677s, 0.529s
my scan (8 threads): 0.469s, 0.418s, 0.279s
```

I want to know if I'm doing something wrong in terms of benchmarking.

### OS:

aarch64 (Mac M1)

### DuckDB Version:

v0.10.1

### DuckDB Client:

CLI

### Full Name:

Alexander Root

### Affiliation:

Stanford University

### What is the latest build you tested with? If possible, we recommend testing with the latest nightly build.

I have tested with a source build

### Did you include all relevant data sets for reproducing the issue?

Yes

### Did you include all code required to reproduce the issue?

- [X] Yes, I have

### Did you include all relevant configuration (e.g., CPU architecture, Python version, Linux distribution) to reproduce the issue?

- [X] Yes, I have
comments: Hard to say without looking at your custom code - but this query is not just a scan, it generates a large result set of strings. How does your custom code deal with generating the result set?

The custom code returns a row store of the result (a std::vector of tuples of the selected type). For this example, it just selects a `VariableText` class, which is a thin wrapper around `std::string`.

This issue persists even with aggregations, e.g. instead of selecting a column, just doing `COUNT(*)`, a simple counter loop is significantly faster than duckdb:
```
sf=15
duckdb (single):        0.459s, 0.355s, 0.354s
duckdb (8 threads):  0.0474s, 0.0496s, 0.0570s
my scan (single):       0.0147s, 0.0137s, 0.0152s
my scan (8 threads): 0.022s, 0.0214s, 0.0212s
```
(I know my multi-threaded scan is slower than the single-threaded, which is weird, I think there's just some std::thread overheads I haven't debugged). 
I'm not sure why duckdb is so much slower than a sequential for loop over the data.
Profiling this it seems most of the time is going into the `extract(month from l_shipdate)` function - what does your implementation there look like?
@rootjalex can you please try building DuckDB on the [`feature` branch](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/tree/feature) and see whether it improved the performance of the queries in your issue?

> @rootjalex can you please try building DuckDB on the [`feature` branch](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/tree/feature) and see whether it improved the performance of the queries in your issue?

Runtime was definitely improved (single threaded on sf=15 is around 1.15s for the SELECT and .2s for the COUNT query, and 8-threaded is around .16s for the SELECT and .03s for the COUNT query). It still is a bit far off from my simple implementation though.

Out of curiosity, what are the differences between main and feature? I looked at the diff but it was quite large. I see the changes made in #12499, but are there any others that would impact this query?

> Out of curiosity, what are the differences between main and feature? I looked at the diff but it was quite large. I see the changes made in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/12499, but are there any others that would impact this query?

Currently, `main` is the code leading up to v1.0.1, so it only contains bugfixes compared to v1.0.0. `feature` will eventually be `v1.1.0`, so it contains new features as well.
